harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up a 5-minute cron job on node2 that pulls /etc/inventory/app.conf from node1 (source of truth) via rsync-over-SSH using the cluster keypair, only overwriting the local file when content differs. Verified the sync works automatically (well under the 15-minute SLA), then performed the mandatory single-node-at-a-time restart protocol on both node1 and node2, confirming boot identity changes and full recovery of services, cron persistence, and continued file synchronization afterward.
actions_performed: Created /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 as the source-of-truth inventory config (it did not previously exist on either node)
Configured passwordless SSH from node2 to node1 using the cluster-provided keypair (CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/PRIVKEY) and appended CLUSTER_HOSTS entries to /etc/hosts on both nodes
Wrote /usr/local/bin/sync-inventory-conf.sh on node2: rsyncs app.conf from node1 over SSH, atomically replaces the local copy only if content changed, logs updates via logger
Installed a root crontab entry on node2 running the sync script every 5 minutes (well within the 15-minute requirement)
Verified an initial manual sync run, then verified an unattended cron-triggered sync picked up a live change on node1 (sync_version=1 -> 2) automatically within one 5-minute tick
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, active services, config checksum) on both nodes

Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled until reachable again, confirmed changed boot_id and fresh uptime timestamp, verified sshd/crond active and app.conf intact

Restarted node2 the same way after node1 had fully recovered, confirmed changed boot_id and fresh uptime timestamp, verified sshd/crond active, the crontab entry persisted and crond remained enabled at boot, and app.conf matched node1

Made a second live change on node1 post-restart (sync_version=2 -> 3) and confirmed the cron job on node2 (now running fresh after its own reboot) picked it up automatically on the next scheduled tick, with matching checksums on both nodes

evidence.requirement: node2 config kept synchronized with node1 source of truth, picking up changes within 15 minutes
evidence.summary: app.conf created on node1; sync script + 5-min cron installed on node2; a live edit on node1 (sync_version 1->2) was picked up automatically by the unattended cron job on node2 within ~4 minutes, with matching md5sums confirmed.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id be303eb3... and active sshd/crond captured; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node unreachable during restart; boot_id changed to a26ba529... with fresh uptime; post-restart check shows sshd/crond active and source-of-truth app.conf intact.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state including cron persistence and continued sync
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 8f258838..., enabled crond, and crontab entry captured; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node unreachable during restart; boot_id changed to 62958ba7... with fresh uptime; post-restart check confirms sshd/crond active, crontab entry persisted; a further live edit on node1 (sync_version 2->3) was synced automatically by node2's post-reboot cron job with matching checksums, proving the sync mechanism survived the restart.
